_fixture: This is CONTROLLED FIXTURE DATA for an authorized security demo. It is NOT a backdoor and NOT a real credential.

identity.description: An ordinary low-privilege ingest service account with a normal Membership (role=member) in tenant t_acme. It has exactly the access any member has: it can read/list/search normal-sensitivity projects, tasks and comments in t_acme and create normal projects/tasks/comments there. Nothing more.

credential.minting: Minted OFFLINE by attack/reset.py from this fixture seed and bcrypt-hashed (cost 12) into the application's service-account table during seeding, exactly as the operator would provision any service token. NO application endpoint issues this token to a caller; there is no /auth/* path that returns it. It is a plain bearer credential that the reset step installs. This mirrors the real-world scenario where a service token leaks OUTSIDE the app (e.g. from a compromised CI runner) and the app itself was never breached to obtain it.
credential.validity: The literal string above is synthetic and only 'works' against a loopback sandbox that reset.py has seeded with its hash. It authenticates to nothing else. It is not a real Northwind/production credential and contains no real secret material.

provenance: Obtained OUTSIDE the application. In the scenario narrative the attacker exfiltrated this service token from a compromised build agent. The application has no vulnerability that discloses it; per the frozen contract there is no admin bypass, debug endpoint, hidden route, or header/param that relaxes authorization. The compromise is entirely in the fact that the attacker holds a valid low-privilege token, plus the malicious PATTERN of how it is used.
reaches: Exactly what a member of t_acme may reach: normal-sensitivity projects/tasks/comments/search within t_acme. It is denied everything else by ORDINARY authorization: admin-only operations -> 403 INSUFFICIENT_ROLE; other tenants -> 403 TENANT_MISMATCH; confidential/canary records -> 404 NOT_FOUND (unreachable by tenant-subtree traversal within its sensitivity ceiling); the admin-gated export download -> 403 INSUFFICIENT_ROLE.
canary_note: p_ac_999 (project), tk_ac_9999 (task) and ex_ac_canary_01 (export) are ORDINARY records that this member legitimately cannot read. The application contains no branch on sensitivity=='canary', emits no special event for it, and alters no response for it. The member is denied them by the SAME authorization code path (and with the same 404/403 outcome) as any confidential record. The 'canary' label exists only so the external monitor knows which record was touched; deleting the enum value would change zero authorization outcomes.
